label: Blue
description: Blue in interiors: Feels calm, slightly distant and airier than warm colours of equal depth.
intro: Blue appears across 1 product family and 2 options, especially on Rugs.
theory: Blue is a receding colour in most interiors, which is why it calms large forms and can make a piece feel visually lighter than the same object in orange or red.
Its biggest variable is saturation. Dusty blue reads almost neutral, while clean bright blue behaves like an accent and needs tighter editing around it.
palette: For a quiet scheme, pair blue with beige, soft white and warm timber. That creates warm-cool balance without dramatic contrast.
For more energy, use the classic complementary idea: controlled blue with touches of rust, cognac or muted orange. Keep the warm note as an accent, not a second dominant field.

profileRows.label: Undertone
profileRows.value: Can range from greyed denim tones to clearer marine and petrol notes.

profileRows.label: Visual effect
profileRows.value: Feels calm, slightly distant and airier than warm colours of equal depth.

profileRows.label: Works well with
profileRows.value: beige, white, warm oak, rust and camel

profileRows.label: Balancing move
profileRows.value: Warm materials such as oak, cognac and sand stop blue interiors from turning cold.
